places.name: East End Brewing Company
places.description: Craft brewery with a patio & an in-house pizza kitchen, plus a variety of beer, cider & soda pop.
places.narrative: A beloved Larimer craft brewery pulling a 4.8 from nearly 500 reviews, with an in-house pizza kitchen and what reviewers call "a large outside seating area" plus plenty of indoor space when weather turns. Photos show burgers, tacos, and plated dishes alongside that deck — so food goes well beyond just pizza. Dog-friendly, beer/cider/soda lineup means everyone finds something (though no cocktails or wine — beer-focused all the way). The catch: closed today (Sunday), so bookmark this one. Just 3 min from Squirrel Hill.

reviews.text: Came to East End Brewing for some late night beer and snacks. Everything was good and the place was pretty cool. They have a large outside seating area and plenty of space inside for when it’s cold.

This small, anemic twist of dough with a little cup of cheese sauce was $8. Disgusting and absurd. The drinks are solid, but the food here is horrendous. Pizza is so-so, veggie soup is nearly inedible, pickled veggies are bitter and mushy, “pretzels” are clearly not alkali washed and underbaked.

Lovely outdoor space, it’s a shame the food is so awful. Go here for drinks, but get dinner elsewhere.
Pizza and beer are definitely worth the trek!  I don’t usually like thick / square pizza - but theirs definitely is an exception.  The West Coast IPA is fantastic.

I have been to East End a number of times over the years, and really thought I had reviewed them before, but obviously not. This is a well ran bar and pizza restaurant that always has an inviting feel to it that makes you feel comfortable spending time having a drink or some food and chatting.

On this last visit on a random Saturday afternoon, I fiest tried their Anniversary Dopplebock, which was a strong and intense, but altogether enjoyable beer. I then tried the Central Business District, one of the last entries in their 5 year project for nearly 100 different beers named for and dedicated to different Pittsburgh neighborhoods, which is a really cool endeavor. The beer itself had a unique herbal quality to it, and was a fun and different pilsner. My wife tried their hard lemonade, which unsurprisingly blows something like "Mike's" out of the water, and she really enjoyed it.

Add in an always pleasant staff and nice outdoor area that can be enjoyed by kids and furry friends, and you have a great local establishment that is worth a stop if in the area and craving a good beer and/or some hearty pizza.

East End Brewing has always been a pleasant spot to get together for drinks and pizza. The staff is kind, the ambiance is warm, and service is smooth. The bartender Keri is really helpful, personable and knowledgeable; she knows what's good lol. She recommended the Roots Mule, and it is the best alcoholic beverage I've ever had on tap - if you like ginger, definitely come to East End Brewing and try it!

reviews.text: LOVE this place. The staff is always super nice. We love Holly, John, Jason, Laci, and Gina are fantastic.  This is after 2 years of visiting. And the outdoor space is phenomenal. More than enough room for large groups. Also the beer is great, always. They have sours and ciders too. They deserve to be way busier than they are. Very dog friendly and have a fire going as well on cold days. YOU NEED LIVE MUSIC or a DJ on sundays. PLEASE
Good servers, atmosphere, lots of space to hangout inside and out. Dog friendly. I’m not a beer person, but liked that they had alternative options, I liked / got the seltzer mimosa.

Second visit to this location, last time was in 2022 when I was in town. Beer was very good and ended up getting a 4 pack of the Dark Nectar (honey porter) to go. Owner gave me a to go cooler bag to keep the beer cold, much appreciated. I’ll definitely be back and if you haven’t been get there you will enjoy the atmosphere and beers. Cheers.

The staff at Grist house is excellent, just like the beer they serve.  They are always focused on the customers and treat everyone with respect and kindness.  Holly has really shown in her short time as a shift leader with natural abilities to lead and stay focused on the customers.  My favorite brewery in Pittsburgh and an excellent staff with Gina, John, Jason, Laci, Kelsey and Hailey.  All top notch brewtenders, slinging delicious beers.  Great place to stop for a relaxing and attentive time.

Best brewery in the city of Pittsburgh best sours, and everything great atmosphere the fire Pitts and everything outside!
I come here every weekend right now they have my favorite beer in Stock!!

places.description: Tiki bar serving Polynesian-inspired cocktails & bar snacks in tropical surrounds.
places.narrative: Not a brewery but a tiki bar right on Shady Ave, just 2 min away, serving Polynesian-inspired cocktails in tropical surrounds. Reviewers note "food selection is limited, but pairs with the drinks nicely" — think bar snacks rather than full meals. The drinks are the real draw and reportedly "make for great photos." Carissa would love the atmospheric vibe, and the full drink menu (beer, cocktails, wine) means everyone's covered. Closed today (Sunday) though, so plan a weeknight visit to this neighborhood gem.

reviews.text: A bit overpriced, but that's what you get for going to a tiki bar. Excellent drinks with even more excellent glasses, mugs, and other vessels. Food selection is limited, but pairs with the drinks nicely. Drinks make for great photos.

This place is really cute and the server was really really nice. The automatic 20% gratuity for all checks is a little bizarre. I do love tipping well, but that was pretty weird to feel so forced… The drinks are all served in really really cute ways (so many points for creativity!) but all three drinks that I got a chance to try were kind of terrible. The food was very ok… The only reason I would come back is because the ambience is cool, the people are nice, and the drinks are cute… I would never order another one for myself, but they are cool to look at!

The drinks are delicious, but what really keeps me coming back is the impeccable service. Heads up - there is a 20% auto gratuity, but the bartender let us know beforehand and I tipped him extra on top of that anyways because he deserved it. If you’re looking for a good spot for a drink in Pittsburgh, I could not recommend this place more. There’s a wide variety of options for everybody, including a couple mocktails on the menu for those who don’t drink/play designated driver.

A must for any true tiki enthusiast. The cocktails are phenomenal, the food is fantastic, and the environment is immersive and fun. Andrea, the head bartender, takes pride in her work. You can't go wrong with anything here.

Awesome bar! As a tiki enthusiast, I found that the drinks are spectacular: well balanced and varied. The Ride or Die was phenomenal. Garnishes and mugs on point.

In addition to delightful alcoholic options, they had a few NA options as well; all three that we tried were amazing. We grabbed a few food items and they were delicious as well.

All the servers were so nice, environment was clean and pleasant. Just overall a lovely evening; wish I lived closer! (Visited while traveling out of town)

places.name: Two Frays Brewery
places.narrative: A Garfield brewery with a 4.8 rating and creative brews — reviewers highlight a watermelon-and-kiwi conditioned pale ale that sounds adventurous. Here's the key detail: a reviewer flatly states "they don't have food, but you are welcome to bring in food." So this is BYOF territory — grab takeout from somewhere great and pair it with their craft beer on the patio. Open RIGHT NOW until 8 PM, just 4 min away. The bring-your-own-food policy actually makes this flexible if you want to control the menu.

reviews.text:
Cute neighborhood craft brewery that fits perfectly in the Garfield neighborhood of Pittsburgh.

They had 11 beers on tap when we visited, as well as ciders, wines and other alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages.  We tried the Better Together Kolsch Style Ale and the Everybody Should Be Nice to Everyone a pale malt and wheat then conditioned on watermelon and kiwi.  They have 2-3 sizes depending upon the beer's ABV.

No, they dont have food, but you are welcome to bring in food. I swear everyone had a pizza or snack from a nearby restaurant.

There is seating inside or on a really cool patio area.  Visit their website to view a ton of information about the beers, space, specials and philosophy.  Two Frays has created an inclusive space where good people can enjoy good beer and fellowship together.

Great little neighborhood brewery with a friendly staff. Nice indoor space with an awesome outdoor patio. The variety of beers on this trip was super on point. They had something for everyone. Even if you're not a beer fan, they had something for you: wine, non alcoholic, and a mixed drink (even dog treats for your pup!). No food on location, but you can bring your own, and there's lots of good food around the area.

I had one of their Kolsh beers and it was tasty! Very cool place and extremely inclusive as well. They have a decent size outdoor area where about half is covered with some heat lamps. They said they enclose the outdoor area with plastic to keep the heat in. So it seems they have some extra space for winter as well.

Truly had the time of my life, the staff and even the head Brewer or respectful caring and passionate about what they do.

Truly enjoyed the tour of the brewery.

A really fun space to chill and be great outdoors as well.

Did I mention they allow you to bring in your own food from the local restaurants.

Spak Brothers Pizza is a few doors down and paired nicely with the beer menu here

Amazing place would give 10 Stars if possible wouldn't change a thing.

Two Frays is easily one of Pittsburgh’s standout breweries. The beer is top-notch—thoughtfully brewed with a variety of styles to explore. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, making it a great spot to hang out with friends or wind down after a long day. The staff is friendly and knowledgeable about the beer they serve. If you're looking for a great local brewery experience in Pittsburgh, Two Frays should be on your list.

places.description: Craft brews & modern American eats are the draw at this open, airy gastropub with a cool atmosphere.
places.full_address: 216 S Highland Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15206, USA
places.narrative: Open right now until 3 PM and just 2 min away — this Shadyside gastropub is the closest open option with the full package. Photos show a solid outdoor setup with umbrella-covered sidewalk seating and a partially covered patio area. Reviewers praise the attentive service, with one highlighting server Megan's "great recommendations." Craft brews, cocktails, wine, AND coffee on the menu plus nearly 2,000 reviews at 4.5 stars makes this reliable. Photos show burgers and grain bowls — modern American that should work around the family's dietary needs. Full bar means Robbie gets his cocktails and Jess gets her IPA.

reviews.text: We had such a nice time here! Came on a Tuesday, got seated right away and had amazing service by Megan! She was friendly, attentive and gave us great recommendations. Our drinks were always full and the food came out so fast! Everything was delicious and the happy hour prices were amazing, we can’t wait to come back!

Everything was wonderful! Food and drinks were created uniquely and prepared perfectly. Lizzie was excellent! She was well versed on every beer, cocktail and food item! We will return on our next visit!
We had the best time at tinis and tats! Luke was such a great server and very attentive and helpful. The food was delicious and the atmosphere was even better, a perfect halloween night!

Absolutely hands down one of the best Happy Hours in Pittsburgh. They have an amazing beer selection, and the bartenders, River and Jordan, always knock it out of the park with the mixed drinks. The drinks can be complicated, but they always taste and look so good that it keeps me coming back.

The Urban Tap, with all the charm and industrial flair of a modern Soho apartment, excels in their culinary endeavors. Flavor abounds in their selections; I have yet to find a meal that fails to please or surprise.

Sometimes, lapses will happen, as they can at many places. I had a staff person cater so much to a customer that phoned in that a line formed behind me, full of displeased stares and disappointed grumbles.

All in all, an excellent adventure in Shadyside, worthy of the embarkation.

I was not a fan of the spaetzel nor the potato salad, and the ketchup curry on the fries was more like just ketchup. This place is still totally an option for us when we are in this part of town.

Came here for the first time this past weekend and can’t believe I haven’t been sooner! Great space in Homestead. Tried a few of the draft beers which were quite tasty. We ordered off the food menu and tried the Chicken Döner Kebab and the crinkle cut fries. The sandwich was okay, but lacked enough sauce and the bread to filling ratio was off, fries were decent.  Our neighbors at the bar got the smash burgers and they looked awesome. There was a DJ there and even though it was too cold to sit outside, they have a great outdoor space!

tl;dr VISIT: GOOD food and beer options in a welcoming vibe.

places.name: Jackworth Ginger Beer
places.narrative: The highest-rated ginger beer specialist on the list at 4.9 stars, with reviewers calling it "the greatest bar/tavern/pub I've patronized in recent memory" and praising the cool interior and great staff. Just 3 min from Squirrel Hill and open today until 9 PM. The ginger beer focus makes this unique — a different flavor profile than your typical craft brewery. No food details in the evidence, so check ahead or plan to bring your own. At 77 reviews it's still intimate and under the radar. Worth a visit for something genuinely different.

evidence.text: The inside is really cool and staff are great
It’s been the greatest bar/tavern/pub I’ve patronized in recent memory
Jackworth is a great spot for the whole crew due it's selection of both alcoholic and NA options

reviews.text: Jackworth Ginger Beer, PA’s only ginger beer brewery, crafts crisp, sharp, and boldly flavored ginger beer. We got a few mixed drinks including the classic Moscow mule. The inside is really cool and staff are great. Jackworth has a cozy atmosphere so you can hang out here and have drinks for hours.

Come for the spicy ginger beer, or grab a beer and a fernet. The alcoholic ginger beer has a bit of a strange aftertaste, and the cocktails are just okay. The crew, though, is solid — friendly and down-to-earth.

Jackworth Ginger Beer is a singular experience. This is not the flat, flavorless soda water others peddle as ginger beer. Jackworth Ginger Beer is spicy, tasty, and refreshing. It's a cut above, and deserves all the praise it gets. At the bar, they'll mix it up in cocktails (all good) or you can take it to-go in cans to impress your friends at your next cocktail party.

Amazing. Simply amazing. I was a fan of ginger and a fan of alcohol. But this is not a mere mix of the two. The product is unique and peerless.

This establishment could easily be mistaken for a super chic, pretentious high artisan sign of gentrification, but no. There is an old-fashioned appeal, authentic yet forward-thinking and modern. Tyler, who was tending bar, explained that they use classical techniques in their process, maintaining an authentic approach. All done in house.

The drinks are exceptional. Nothing is as crisp and refreshing as that OG JGB. The ginger flavor is strong but perfectly balanced with the mild sweetness of the beverage. The 0 proof original seems markedly sweeter than the OG JGB, offering a distinct flavor profile. The spicy 0 proof is bomb, delivering a satisfying kick. I only wish I could enjoy a hot summer day with a spicy alcoholic JGB, but it doesn’t exist… yet.

The bar itself has an inviting vibe. It’s been the greatest bar/tavern/pub I’ve patronized in recent memory. The atmosphere is relaxed, with a genuine charm that sets it apart from other places.

If you couldn’t tell, I’m super impressed and generally am critical to a point of fault. However, I don’t have a bad thing to say at all. I will be back.

Jackworth is a great spot for the whole crew due it's selection of both alcoholic and NA options. Most offerings feature their ginger beer (which is amazing), but you can get some other really great drinks as well! It's a laid back spot with really cool, and very nice people working the bar!

My favorite is the spicy ginger beer, but drinker beware, it is in fact very spicy! It packs the most ginger spice that I've ever had and I love it!

reviews.text:
Eleventh Hour is a hidden gem off the main drag of Lawrencville. They offer a nice selection of beers and a chill atmosphere. I first came here for one of their popular trivia nights and had a great time with friends. They always putting together fun activities!

I researched dozens of places in Pittsburgh to host an event and decided to go with Eleventh Hour from my prior experiences. They have a nice large room off the main bar that has dozens of barrels and hanging lights. We brought in minimal decor and had an incredible atmosphere. Brian answered all the questions I had over several weeks and worked with me on some special requests to make the day perfect. A great place to grab or beer or host an event in Pittsburgh!

Awesome spot not far from the strip district, yet far more quiet and featuring quite vast amount of space both indoors and outside.

Brewery often has a food truck, but is walking distance from other food options if you want something from a different menu.

Beers are great, and I would say rival and best some across the river from Dancing Gnome. I am a fan of a NEIPA and their options feature a greatly hazy and full of flavor profile.

This brewery also mails the classics such as their malty Maibock and refreshing Kölsch!

I recommend the trip, great stuff!
Halloween was my first time here and it was awesome. Loved everything, will definitely be returning!
Nice outdoor area. Has a good bar vibe. We sat inside at the open window bar.  Hubby got their Kolsch.  We both liked its smooth taste.

Excellent beer! Plenty of options, three tasters to try different styles. The rice lager was great and my aunt really enjoyed the west coast style IPA despite not normally liking hoppy beer. Cute outside patio, very shady.

I forgot what the name was. The food was okay, but not particularly impressive. What stood for me was definitely the ambience, which was the perfect mix of cozy yet lively. This place has such potential and wish this place the best.

Take the required 20% tip off.  A required tip isn’t a tip - it’s the price.

In general - has an urban upper middle class feel w upscaled bar-leaning American food.  It’s nice quality.   The larger vibe is cozy and close and kinda works.

The servers and waitstaff were also kind, truly helpful, and accommodating.

However, don’t force charge me 20% extra - and even further - only tell me when I get the bill

This company has a history of morally grey stuff like this.  Hidden Harbor next door - same company, same kitchen - used to give you a bill w auto 20% included, hiding that it’s added to the bill under three pieces of paper. You saw a bill w one total number, w no mention of tip. It still had an audacious line to ‘add your tip’!   More!   Server of course not mentioning anything.  I will never forget it.

You want to add a required cost?  Add it to the price, be honest about it.

At the end, I feel mixed, it’s a fine establishment on the surface level stuff, but at the end, I find myself avoiding places like this

Fair warning: German fare runs heavy on cheese and rich sauces, which is tricky for Carissa and Ashi's dietary needs. Southworks side neighborhood is great area to stay when in Pittsburgh

reviews.text: We went there on Saturday afternoon for the crispy pork knuckles( I don’t remember what’s called but they’re going so fast) and Hefe Weizen Mango flavor. We also had pretzel as an appetizer and everything was good 😊

Fun atmosphere and place to have drinks and have food with friends and family. They had live music when which was cool! The potato pancakes were very very deep fried were not the best but the pierogies were pretty good. The fried onions were different not bad but probably would ask for them without the onions. Also the service was good.

Southworks side neighborhood is great area to stay when in Pittsburgh. We went in Hofbrauhaus for drinks, place was quite and performer playing for diners. We dined on the patio , enjoyed bier, wine, and small bites. By the time we made our way out, place was packed and great vibes with live music and songs. Great flavors of bier and wines were good too. View of the Monongahela river was icing on the top!! Place has all the fun vibes, come and enjoy regardless of group size. They even have a separate area for special events.

I have been here before for regular dinner service and the food is always really tasty. Most recently I was here for an event, the food was supposed to be appetizers but it was more than plenty and tons of variety, plus dessert. I had a cocktail recommended by one of the servers and it was delicious. I know they have a great selection of beer too but I don't drink beer too often. The service is always great.

A nice German-style tavern. Lot's of room even for larger parties. The beer was good, but the food could have been better. The quality of the sausage meat & spices was not of the highest caliber. It was still decent though and the sauerkraut was very good.

places.description: Industrial brewery taproom pouring craft beers in inviting digs with a view of the production area.
places.narrative: An industrial-chic Sharpsburg taproom where you can watch the production floor while you drink — the kind of place beer nerds pilgrimage to. Reviewers confirm "seating inside and outside" and note food comes from the resident Blue Sparrow Bus food truck — photos show plated meals with rice, meat, and vegetables. The exterior shot at dusk shows people gathering near barrels and string lights, a nice vibe. At 4.6 stars with 603 reviews, open today until 8 PM, 8 min out. evidence.text: The building itself is very nice with seating inside and outside
If you are hungry they have food from the resident food truck, the Blue Sparrow Bus
Visited here to beat the frigid cold

reviews.text: Dancing Gnome is a top-notch brewery in Sharpsburg. They have many quality beers on tap. The building itself is very nice with seating inside and outside. If you are hungry they have food from the resident food truck, the Blue Sparrow Bus.
Visited here to beat the frigid cold. Had a great afternoon drinking, playing games, and enjoying the food. Would highly recommend this place to anyone in the Pittsburgh area.

This review is long overdue.

The atmosphere is super inviting.  Clean, plenty of space. Nice outdoor space too. The keep everything well maintained and the space is very thoughtful. Great merch.  They make it easily to bring food or utilize their food trucks.  Love that they have a little propagation station.  I do wish the acoustics were slightly better as it does very quickly get a bit too loud especially when the doors are down. I also wish there was slightly more seating and also a few extra tables that are a bit more accessibility/mobility friendly.

I disagree with some of the other reviews on here and recommend giving it a shot vs going based on the reviews.

I value my dog the most over everything and would it be nice to pop in quickly after a long walk, sure, but I’d never fault them for not being dog friendly. I’ve been at breweries where people bring unfriendly dogs, where dogs have knocked things over etc.  Dancing Gnome is also right by a busy street - not the most ideal place to bring a dog.  Their policy has always been clear - posted on their website and on signage out front.

I’ve gone to Dancing Gnome many times with babies or toddlers.  I’ve never had a bad experience. They have a family bathroom with a changing table and staff has always been engaging with the kids. We have always respected that while they allow kids it is still a brewery and the focus is on adults so we make sure to bring something to entertain the kids and make sure they aren’t too loud to bother others. They make their policy about kids clear on their website as well.

I’ve always had really good experiences with staff. They are open to explaining, giving recommendations, etc.  have always been greeted, quickly, and with a smile.

I’ve never had a bad beer there though some might not be for me/my favorite. They are very IPA inspired.

Dancing Gnome is always very thoughtful with their charitable donations. They do A LOT in the community, often a lot that most people don’t know about as they aren’t over the top with communicating about it.  Just really strong community partners. Andrew is kind, not pretentious and cares about putting out great products.

Comfortable ambience and music on a gorgeous fall afternoon.  We stopped in for the Fest/Märzen season beers and thoroughly enjoyed both! Our bartender was really friendly and struck up a conversation with us while we sipped our beers at the bar.  Grab a bite from Blue Sparrow while you session. Great experience all around!

Every beer I tried was very well done. I do wish they had a little more variety on tap though. The service was excellent! I like the openness and size of the inside. I like the logo and brick exterior of the original building better though.

The early 8 AM open is unusual for a brewery — they do coffee and brunch too, making this versatile. Open today until 9 PM, just 5 min away. At 4.5 stars from 396 reviews, Trace punches above its weight. The combination of outdoor hangout vibes and extended hours makes this one of the most practical picks on the list for a Sunday.

I dig this place. There was a Kellerbier on tap, and although not my go-to style, this beer was excellent! I also enjoyed the sour and the Bourbon barrel aged imperial stout with vanilla. This weekend I was supporting queer, women and black owned breweries. Cheers! 🍻

Trace is a brewery that not only offers a fantastic product, but always a warm and welcoming experience. My husband and I live right outside of Philadelphia and ALWAYS make it a point to stop at Trace when we're back in the area visiting family. Em is an absolute gem who provided us with a 10/10 experience. Very knowledgeable & welcoming. We always look forward to our next trip back to Pitt to be able to bring some of Trace back home to share!

2nd year catering a Holiday Party here.  When I came in to clean up this morning, I was offered a cup of coffee, which I gladly accepted.   He asked what kind of coffee I liked, he asked a few questions about my preference and I went about finishing my cleanup. On in my way out we chatted a little bit about the different kinds of beers offered and he handed me a cup of the most delicious cup of mocha coffee I ever tasted in my life.  Thank you made Em, you truley made my day with that perfectly crafted cup of love.

3.5/5

Atmosphere 4.5/5 cool building nice patio intimate fireplace. Warm and cozy feeling.
We parked on the street but might be tough if they get busy dunno if there's much available locally?
Overall I'd go here again and recommend it if someone was in the area and looking to try something new. Don't know that I'll be going out of my way to return.

Allegheny City Brewing offers a fantastic experience with a large selection of in-house craft beers, friendly staff, and a charming atmosphere. They have rotating food trucks throughout the week and are dog friendly!

Outdoors they have a fire pit and a complementary hot chocolate station on colder nights. This place is very dog friendly as well - they have dog treats available at the bar. In addition to their wonderful beers, they also have cocktails and cider on tap. Great place to hang out with friends or grab a drink before heading to dinner.

The best family owned brewery around. Great drinks and great people. Overall, just a happy and fun place to be. Kid and dog friendly. Always have the best food trucks and live music. Truly a very special community spot.

reviews.text:
I've been here twice now, and I'll summarize by saying great atmosphere, great food, poor service.

The atmosphere is to die for, pictures don't do it justice. The warm lighting and music choices add to it as well. The food is fantastic, everything from perogies to French onion soup are great. But both times I went, the service was as if I was a problem for showing up. Wait times were slow, and waitstaff inattentive and disinterested in my asks. If they're overworked, I get it. Otherwise, the service level is getting in the way of the otherwise amazing experience.

Came here for dinner with the family. Everyone enjoyed their meals and the portions are large. The wings had a maple mustard sauce, different but really good. Peirogis were fantastic. I enjoyed the Kobe beef cheesesteak. It was decent, but being from Philly, I am hard judge on cheesesteaks.

Had a great experience at The Church Brew Works. The food was excellent — fresh, flavorful, and came out hot. The beer was great as well, lots of good options and everything I tried was solid.

Our server Mecca was polite, kind, and very attentive the entire time, which made the experience even better. Great service, thanks Mecca!!

The interior was clean and well-kept, including the tables and dining area. Even the bathroom was spotless, which says a lot about how well the place is taken care of. This place has huge potential as a brewery and I cannot wait to stop in in the future!!

Definitely recommend stopping in if you’re in the area! Will be coming back. 🍻

During the entire trip in Pittsburgh they had the best food. Very high level.

The chorizo meatballs were so moist and so delicious with ricotta.

Their pretzel with cheese was very good.

And their pierogies were amazing.

*** The Philly cheesesteak was not that great*** It needed a layer of mayonnaise in between the meat and the meat was way overdone.
This was a great place to get drinks and appetizers to share. Unique atmosphere. Large drink menu with history of the building in the back. Friendly service.

Photos show loaded nachos and tacos with colorful presentation. At 4.6 stars with 293 reviews, the smaller review count suggests a more local, less scene-y crowd. Open until 8 PM today, 7 min out. If you want good beer and solid food without fighting for a table, this is a smart choice — especially for Jess's low-key preference.

the 4 stars is because I really wanted to play darts but they have the old school dart boards. I cant drink some brews AND do math!
The pool tables were beautiful too. gorgeous old wood.
This place is a nice quiet vibe on a Thursday!

Let me say that this brewery has a lot of IPAs: that is a positive for me. They let us taste around 5 different beers before we made a decision. We got a few beers and started with nachos. The nachos were good, a bit pricey, but good. We didn’t love the beer cheese so I wouldn’t start with this again. Their menu has a lot so no concerns.

We decided to get their Yinser Cheesesteak and I would get it again. It was big, the cheesesteak was very good (slightly on the sweet side). The only way to improve this meal is grill the bun but that is preference.

The place was slightly loud in the main room but they have a lot of space to spread out; there are other areas you can go to for large groups or groups that want a quieter environment.

The key…I WILL BE HERE AGAIN.

Great service. The bartender was very friendly. The food was amazing. The buffalo mac and cheese was out of this world. The beer was amazing. We will definitely be back.
Hop Farm has been one of my Favorite breweries for years, however I’ve never posted a review! Great service, beer and yummy burgers ! Plus the space is spacious with beautiful wood details!

Enjoyed the warm ambiance. Was in a hurry to see show at thunderbird. Got my burger whipped out faster than a pittsburgher hitting an on camp with a hockey game to catch lol
Was in from out of town. Smash burger was probably one of the best burgers I’ve ever had no joke. Had a great couple beers on tap. If you’re not giving this place 5 stars check your head.

Stopped in for a beer and a game of pool, but stayed for the hospitality. Jesse and Brandon took care of us and were very friendly. Great place and easily a top 5 burger in Pittsburgh. Definitely stop by if you’re in Lawrenceville.

Nice restaurant.  Has laid back vibe, bar games like pool table, darts and small video game area.  Food definitely not your chain restaurant fair.  Had the mushroom burger which was very good.  The capri sun cocktail was not overly tasty but did come in a cute drink pouch

Photos show a charming beer garden with gravel, red umbrellas, and picnic tables under open sky. Reviewers are sparse — one notes "outside seems nice in season" and another is uncertain about the food situation. This is very much a come-for-the-beer nano-brewery. Open today until 5 PM only, 6 min away. If you're beer-first and value quality over scene, that near-perfect rating says something. Just don't count on a full food menu — check ahead.

reviews.text:
Knocking 1 off this.

Space is lovely and beer very competent; Italian dry pilsner rivals Golden Age, which is the gold standard of pilsners anywhere AFAIAC.

I didn't get a pic of the barrel-aged panda vut it was as it should be, tho it's not how I roll. Very good experience.

Stout lovely, tho these days I tend toward bourbon-aged stouts.

The problem is when I asked the beer pourer about what she likes, she stated she doesn't drink.

What?

How is that helpful?

Do you get that this business isn't about how you feel about libation? All it does is sell beer. Seems kind of a dumb thing to say. IDGAFF about your booze preferences; help me sort out what I should order, FFS.

Why do I have to follow up with, "Well, what do people like?" It's a Microsoft answer-an intellectually competent answer when an emotionally intelligent response is appropriate. "I don't drink but people like .." or even leave out your lesser appropriate inclinations.

That said, space is comfy. Couches, high stools and var chairs. Outside seems nice in season. Local (?) art. Murals.

I do hope the Hazelwood breweries take off. I will mention this place to my meetup bud who  combines brewery visits with pizza; how this place works into that meta is uncertain but the place down the street with New France and ... and soon to be Abjuration seems to have space for a food truck.

Hazel Grove is definitely one of my favorite brew houses in the Burgh! Their new non-alcoholic brew is incredible, and the rosemary blood orange mocktail is just as impressive. You can truly feel how invested the owners are in the community—they create such a welcoming, inclusive space and are always supporting local collaborations. It’s the kind of place you want to keep coming back to, whether for the drinks, the vibe, or the people behind it all

Really nice brewery that I'm happy to have stumbled upon. When in the Hazelwood area of Pittsburgh to have dinner at The Woods House, I realized this brewery was just down the hill and had some time to kill before my reservation.

The building itself looks rather unassuming, but you can kind of tell by the signage and presentation outside it's a cared for place. Once inside, that notion was proven, as the space was well maintained, sharp overall, adorned with cool wall art and comfortable overall.

My wife and I both got a beer, the brown ale German pils, and the service was pleasant and diligent. The beer itself was very well done, and only made me sad that I could not try more options and that the brewery is pretty far from my home. It's definitely worth a stop when in the area looking for a good beer in an inviting and comfortable space.
What an amazing brewery! Excellent craft beer and an amazing vibe. What more do you need! The beer was excellent, and the service was on point. Hazel Grove is really taking it to the next level!

We had a double birthday party at Hazel Grove Brewing for my 1-year-old grandson and his grandfather in this perfect venue. All ages found something to enjoy: bar games, great beers, gorgeous murals, bright and comfortable surroundings. Even the bathrooms are lovely! Too bad it was winter - the courtyard looked great.
We self-catered, which was perfect for the various food preferences. Welcoming staff, real neighborhood vibe. My daughter and her family live nearby in Greenfield so I know we will be back.

We came for the mac mural and stayed for the vibes. It was so cool being able to walk through the property and view the equipment with a beer in hand. The beer was delicious and the arcade games were a riot. The mac art is most dope.

This place is cool but every beer I've had has been lackluster and the pinball is set to tokens rather than quarters, so you end up with a bunch a useless tokens if you don't use them all after changing up a $20 bill.

Will return to try more beers, but something is just off. Tough to describe.

Cool brewery down in Southside. We popped in here after brunch and were surprised about how big the space is inside. There is a small taproom area, an arcade, and two pickleball courts. I tried the Salty Tomato Club, which was their collab with 412 Food Rescue and it was 10/10. Even took a 4-pack home! Will definitely be back.

Very cool and unique brewery located in a giant warehouse.  Beers are fantastic, but the atmosphere makes it so cool.  Has around 50 pinball machines that are well taken care of, some arcade games, a ping pong table, and several pickle ball courts!

At 4.6 with 2,636 reviews and a full bar (cocktails, wine, coffee, live music), it's a proven crowd-pleaser. Open until 10 PM today but at 11 min away, it's the furthest mainstream pick. Best paired with a North Shore outing or pre/post-game plans.

Bartenders were excellent and were happy to give out samples. Strawberry letter was a surprise! Sour and sweet. Order the Island fish tacos! Also excellent 2 filled me up and took the 3rd to the hotel for a late night snack. Then pineapple coleslaw was a nice surprise. The tacos needed some spice so I asked for some Choulua hot sauce and it was complete! Loved this place!

This is definitely your spot for game day adventures. Didn’t get to try any of the food but it was a standard bar menu. The beer options were expansive and they had drinks for everyone. Heated patio for winter games and open patio for summer time! This is a great place to stop for Steelers Sunday

Stopped by today for the first time and sat at the bar.  Our bar tender, Nick was very attentive and provided us with some samples before we ordered our beer.  We ordered the smoky wings as an appetizer and they were the best wings I’ve had in years, better than any wings in Pennsylvania. The chicken meat was smoked to perfection and the BBQ sauce was on point.  Nick recommended the cheese steak sandwich which was amazing.  The meat was flavorful along with the cheese sauce and the bread had an amazing char flavor to it along with grill marks.  It was a decadent food experience which was made thanks to the suggestions made by our bar tender Nick.  The ambiance was great and we will definitely be back.

Food was good. Interesting crowd…. Came on a Sunday and the Steelers have a home game on Monday… the $5 bites is confusing because we were told it wasn’t valid today….. it’s Sunday and there’s not a home game today…. And they were out of chips and chili.. overall would not come back…. Also 3 of the servers are sitting on their phones at a table behind us while our drinks are empty

I was a first time guest. We were a little late for our reservation due to gps issues. We were greeted by a very friendly girl who took us to our seat. They were very busy so I would suggest a reservation. Our server Miranda was amazing. Very helpful with our drink selections and food. I had the fish tacos and would go back just for that. My sister had a cheeseburger and loved it. Great place, wonderful staff, exceeded expectations.

places.name: The Fire Side Public House
places.description: Traditional pub fare plus beer & cocktails in a straightforward, unfussy setting.
places.narrative: Just 3 min from Squirrel Hill on Broad Street, with one of the most impressive outdoor setups around. Photos show string lights and an outdoor setup, and reviewers love that "you can see your food being made on the fire" — it's a proper fire-grilled pub. Full bar including coffee, open until 9:30 PM today. At 4.3 with 1,183 reviews, the fire-cooked concept gives it a unique edge over standard pub fare. The string-lit patio is a strong contender for evening hangs as the sun goes down. Proximity alone makes this a top pick for a lazy Sunday.

evidence.text: The service was friendly - the place smelled amazing - and it’s pretty cool to be able to see your food being made on the fire
We went on a Wednesday and they had great $5 drink options
Everything we had was delicious, for sure going to go back to try the rest of the menu

reviews.text: We have lived nearby for a while and so happy we finally checked this place out. The service was friendly - the place smelled amazing - and it’s pretty cool to be able to see your food being made on the fire. We went on a Wednesday and they had great $5 drink options. Everything we had was delicious, for sure going to go back to try the rest of the menu.

I got the Pittsburgh steak and fries…. The best part of the meal was the fries, my steak sandwich could have been seasoned, and I never got the cup of tea I ordered… the 2 young ladies at the front counter were nice

We are from our of State and thought the menu looked great on Google.  It was amazing! Waitress was good. The atmosphere was a good, fun vibe. My husband and I sat at the bar and watched them grill food. That was cool. Everything the chefs made looked amazing❣️I had 2 drinks. He had tea since he was driving. Bill was $38 plus our tip.  It's not too bad on price, I thought

Pros: great food for a great price; it's hard to beat the quality for the price here and we enjoyed almost everything we had. The daily deals are great. The wood grill adds a great flavor that not a lot of places do (or if they do, it's expensive). The amount of light in the place is also great, huge windows on all sides just makes for a nice atmosphere -- if you can't sit outside on the patio, you can still at least feel like you're outside. It's also nice to see the wood grill in operation -- just adds to the experience. We also had a great server.

Cons: I really love the decor/layout of the place (see above) but I gave it a 3/5 on atmosphere because of the loudness of the interior. I think it's the fans in the middle that add such a loud background noise... some sound absorbing would help. I would sit outside in nice weather for this reason alone. Additionally, the fries were a little inconsistent (nothing crazy).

My wife and I have been here several times and will go again -- just a solid, unique restaurant with lots to love at a reasonable price.

The food is awesome!!! The wings, the burgers!!! But the servers…. They don’t look at you when you are placing the order…. They don’t give you napkins…. I had to ask like 3 times for drinks… and the place was literally empty…. Next time I ll place an order pick up

places.name: Helltown Brewing - Strip District
places.narrative: A Strip District brewery with the most complete amenity list of any brewery here — cocktails, wine, coffee, beer, live music, AND dog-friendly. Photos show a spacious patio with picnic tables, string lights, and umbrellas, though reviewers warn about limited shade. Reviewers also note a "full cocktail menu" beyond just beer. Photos show restaurant-quality plated entrees. Open until 6 PM today, 7 min away. The Strip location means you could combine this with a market walk. Robbie gets cocktails, Jess gets IPA, everyone wins — just note the early Sunday close and pack sunglasses.

evidence.text: They also have a full cocktail menu
A large outdoor seating space is available, but not much shade
Be aware they do not serve food, but they welcome you to bring outside food to enjoy

reviews.text: All the beers we tried were fantastic. They also have a full cocktail menu. Large space with frequent events (music, trivia, pinball), a row of arcade machines. A large outdoor seating space is available, but not much shade. Be aware they do not serve food, but they welcome you to bring outside food to enjoy.

Cool space in the heart of the Strip District. Lot of beer variety and nice to see multiple NA options.
Band was very overwhelming for the space and did not allow for conversations at the bar or your own table
Would have loved more low profile and comfortable seating options to encourage staying longer

This is a nice spot to stop at in the strip for a beer. It has a large bar inside with plenty of seating, and there is also a large outside patio with a smaller bar that will just serve you drinks. Mixed drinks are also available on site and 4 packs to go. It doesn't appear they have food anymore, as their site says, so be prepared. There are some places around the area you can order from, and they allowed us to bring in outside food.

Ribs were tough, not falling off the bone tender. The strawberry salad was not nearly as good as the strawberry salad at Mod's pizza, Mac and cheese was just ok. The waiter was super nice. The food just didn't live up to the menu description. My husband didn't enjoy his skewered shrimp either. It was so expensive for such disappointing food. Nice atmosphere. Drinks were good.

This was an awesome stop during our Pittsburgh weekend trip. A large outdoor area is available, but we stayed inside and relaxed between the bar and wine tasting zone.

BBQ is available, and the beers were great, with friendly staff and quick service. Would definitely return next time I'm in the area.

places.name: Mondays Brewing Taproom
places.narrative: A brand-new Greenfield addition just 4 min away with a 4.8 rating from only 28 reviews. Photos show a nice raised wooden deck — promising for outdoor hangs. The food situation is evolving: one reviewer notes "the kitchen isn't open yet" and hopes for small plates, so confirm what's available before heading out. Called "a great addition to Greenfield" by locals. Open until 8 PM today. This is a watch-this-space pick — the proximity, the early rating, and the deck setup are all promising, but verify the food before committing.

evidence.text: This is a great addition to have in Greenfield
The kitchen isn't open yet but also hoping they end up getting some small plates or something
They had some popcorn available for snacking and 4 packs to go

reviews.text:
This is a great addition to have in Greenfield. There was a really nice line up of beers and different varieties. The staff was super friendly and welcoming. We had a private event there, and they were very hospitable, and the space was perfect. If you have been to Hough's before, the place has the same layout, but I am looking forward to seeing how it grows. The kitchen isn't open yet but also hoping they end up getting some small plates or something. Overall a good spot to go and have a beer!

They had some popcorn available for snacking and 4 packs to go. There were also some non-alcoholic beverages available.

A lovely place with a variety of craft beer that's been sorely lacking in this neighborhood! Sam graciously opened the back room for us to host a private event with our running club. The service and atmosphere was perfect. I'm excited to see what the vibe is like when the kitchen opens in 2025!

Mondays customer service and atmosphere was great. It was our first time visiting and the beer was good. As someone who just passed the BJCP I was excited to check them out and try a few things. Unfortunately because of the food service connected to them I can’t leave 5 stars. We tried to order some plain fries due to my wife being lactose intolerant and was rudely told no we don’t do that. Which if you can’t leave off the cheese whatever that’s fine but it didn’t need to be said with such a tone like we were attacking the business. Smash n fried could learn from Mondays staff. We would have stayed for more the one beer but the tone the worker had behind the counter soured our experience. I have been in the service industry my entire career and hate leaving reviews but it’s getting old seeing customer service decline.
Mondays helped me host an event in their taproom.  It was the perfect venue, and the drinks from Mondays and food from Smashed'n Fried were amazing.  Great addition to the Greenfield neighborhood.
Such good beer! Particularly liked the Belgian Dubbel and Irish Red. Nice space and slick branding :)

places.name: Coven Brewing
places.narrative: A chill Lawrenceville nano-brewery where reviewers highlight "some of my favorite food trucks on a regular basis" and a relaxed, neighborhood vibe that Jess would appreciate. At 4.6 with 83 reviews, it's intimate and unpretentious. No outdoor photos were captured despite outdoor seating being listed, so the patio situation is a question mark. Open until 6 PM today, 6 min away. Beer-only as far as we can tell. A nice low-key option without the crowd of bigger spots — just check their socials for today's food truck lineup before heading out.

evidence.text: They have some of my favorite food trucks on a regular basis
Great little space in Lawrenceville, love the chill vibe
Nice outdoor space when the weather is nice

reviews.text: Coven is located on butler st in lawrenceville. It’s small in the inside but comfortable. They don’t have a huge selection on tap however most of their beer is delicious, I like their hazy ipas. They have some of my favorite food trucks on a regular basis. Check them out
The Phantom Experience IPA is delicious and could hold its own in Vermont.  Vibe is surprisingly posh for the ‘Burgh.  Open early on Black Friday.
Great little space in Lawrenceville, love the chill vibe. Good selection of beer. Nice outdoor space when the weather is nice. Solid food truck line up.
Great spot for spooky season or any season...  Across from the beautiful cemetery with amazing craft beers on tap.

Solid line of beers at this upstart brewery! The cozy ambience is nice too. Removed one star as they refused to pour even the smallest amount of beer from their draft line to taste in advance. I really am rubbed the wrong way when breweries do this (almost never). That said, the beer we had was delicious (especially their Saison as seen in this pic), and we will be back to Coven.

places.name: Mike's Beer Bar
places.narrative: A North Shore bar and grill where reviewers simply say "the food is absolutely incredible" — strong words backed by 4.5 stars across 1,416 reviews. Photos show loaded nachos, wings, and sides. Outdoor seating is listed but no outdoor photos were found, so verify the patio situation before going specifically for outdoor dining. Dog-friendly, open until midnight today (the latest hours on this entire list), 10 min away. Cocktails and wine available. If you're after a late-night beer-and-food spot after everywhere else closes, this is your play.

evidence.text: Great atmosphere
The food is absolutely incredible
Great local beer selection

reviews.text: This place is phenomenal! First time here for an OSU Buckeyes football game and the place is full of Buckeye fans. Great atmosphere! I imagine the atmosphere for Steelers or Pirates games is crazy. The food is absolutely incredible! And the service is just as good! Awesome beer selection too. Highly, highly recommend!

Loved this place! Great local beer selection! And the steak on a stone was excellent! I was skeptical, but the guy next to me got the Cowboy ribeye so I got the same. It was a bit tricky to finish cooking the  steak on the stone, but got it figured out very quickly and I cooked each piece to my perfection! It was fun! Bring a lens wipe for your glasses, cause you will get some splatter while searing each piece. The steak tasted perfect. Tender and flavorful without being over seasoned. The sweet potatoes fries were delicious also. The bartender and manager were very nice and friendly and the owner was an awesome guy and got to talk to him about his restaurant and his passion shows through.

On a recent August trip to Pittsburgh to see Jays vs Pirates baseball series, we found our spot and we are so happy we did. Mike's Bar is literally across from the stadium. The atmosphere, the food (pickle focaccia pizza, wings, pretzels) & drinks (IC Beer)and of course the amazing staff - Nick, Stana & Summer
Thank you
Alan & Maria
P.S. We will be back...

We wondered in to Mike’s Beer Bar to watch the Steelers game.  We got a table with plenty of TVs around us and they turned the sound to the Steelers game.  Taliyah did a great job suggesting beer and food.  We had the Chilli, Duck&Apple Focaccia Pizza and the Verde Chicken Nachos.  Wish the refs were as good as the food.  We will go back again.

I was so impressed with the food! We got a pickle pizza and a couple burgers. The fries were INCREDIBLE. Taliah was very attentive (it was really busy but she still paid great attention to us, got kids water cups for my children without me having to ask) and she had excellent drink recommendations. We will be back!

places.name: CoStar Brewing
places.narrative: An Etna nano-brewery pulling a remarkable 4.9 from 61 reviews. Reviewers say it "feels like a great neighborhood spot, especially when the weather warms up" and confirm seating on the side of the small building. Photos show a concrete patio with bar-height tables, stools, and patio heaters — charming for how compact it is. Open until 6 PM today, 9 min away. The building is small so expect an intimate, locals-know-about-it vibe. No clear food details in the evidence, so check ahead. That near-perfect rating with 60+ reviews is genuinely impressive for pure beer quality.

evidence.text: This feels like a great neighborhood spot, especially when the weather warms up
The building is small but there is seating inside and outside on the side
You can also get something to eat from the rotating food trucks that park out front

reviews.text: First time stopping in after driving past countless times, and we’ve clearly been missing out. On a blustery January Sunday, we finally made it in and were glad we did. The pours were excellent and the IPAs were right on point. This feels like a great neighborhood spot, especially when the weather warms up. Glad it’s close by and already looking forward to coming back. Keep those hops flowing.

CoStar Brewing is a nice brewery in the heart of Etna. The building is small but there is seating inside and outside on the side. I like the beer they have it was all crisp and refreshing. You can also get something to eat from the rotating food trucks that park out front.

A wonderful brewery with some excellent selections.  They are very chill about bringing your own food so we love to grab takeout and come over here.  They definitely have the best outdoor seating in the area as well.  Dog friendly.

Updated review: They now have a nice outdoor space, and the beer has continued to be solid. This is becoming a regular stop for us. Added a star and some more photos. Make sure to check this place out.

Original review: I am happy to finally see CoStar in a brick and mortar place after having seen their beers in local establishments around the Burgh. The space is small but nice. It truly has that microbrewery feel since you're drinking next to the brewing equipment. They have some plans to make an outside space. This was a soft opening so not a lot of beers available but that cream ale is super solid. Looking forward to visiting again.

We hosted an adult's birthday party here and it couldn't have been better. I worked with Dominic on the party details and he was super accommodating and flexible. Very great experience! The taproom is super cool and a fun space. Our children were entertained by the games and outdoor space which made the day even better.

I think the prices are very reasonable too.

All in all I highly highly recommend Costar for events or just hanging out and having a beer.

places.name: Old Thunder Brewing Company
places.narrative: Out in Blawnox at 12 min away, but that 4.9 rating from 212 reviews suggests it's worth the drive for the right occasion. Reviewers confirm you can "sit inside or outside" with food trucks throughout the week, plus cocktail, cider, and N/A options — more drink variety than most breweries here. No outdoor photos were captured, so the patio vibe is a question mark. Open until 7 PM today. This is a destination brewery where the beer quality clearly speaks for itself. Best for a deliberate outing when you want to explore beyond the usual neighborhoods.

evidence.text: You can sit inside or outside and they have food trucks throughout the week if you get hungry
Also have great cocktail/cider and N/A options if that’s your thing
Super friendly and knowledgeable bartenders make it a great experience every time

reviews.text: Old Thunder is a fantastic brewery located in the heart of Blawnox. They have many high-quality beers on tap including cask beer. The inside is very cozy and modern being in the old post office. You can sit inside or outside and they have food trucks throughout the week if you get hungry.

Old Thunder makes the best beer in the city, hands down! I’ve been a regular since close to the beginning and never had a bad beer here. Also have great cocktail/cider and N/A options if that’s your thing. Super friendly and knowledgeable bartenders make it a great experience every time.

Old Thunder consistently brews the highest quality craft beer in the greater Pittsburgh area.  The staff here is knowledgeable, friendly, and very attentive.  The atmosphere (a revitalized post office) is comfortable and roomy with an option to sit outside.  They also have the best food truck lineup day after day.

Been a huge fan from the beginning. Super friendly and knowledgeable staff. Beer is always on point with a great selection. Easily my favorite brewery in the Pittsburgh area. Beautiful space and nice vibe, nice outdoor seating also available.

Besides the beer they have some Goodlanders cocktails available on tap, if that's your jam. And some seltzers. Food trucks throughout the week.

I’m sad I’ve waited so long to visit OT, but thankful I took the opportunity this weekend. It’s a beautiful and clean space and located in a relatively peaceful neighborhood. The beer is delicious and beertender Max is awesome. Highly recommend if you’re in the Pittsburgh area for a few days.

places.name: Industry Public House
places.description: Elevated comfort food & craft beers star at this brick-walled restaurant with industrial accents.
places.narrative: Elevated comfort food meets craft beer in a brick-walled Lawrenceville industrial-chic space. Reviewers praise knowledgeable staff and note it's great for "late night dinner after a long day." The real draw is the hours: open until 2 AM today — by far the latest full-service option if the night runs long. Full bar with cocktails, wine, and coffee, 6 min away. At 4.2 with 1,825 reviews, it's reliable but not top-tier, and the outdoor situation is modest (partially visible patio in photos). Think of this as your safety net when everywhere else closes early on Sunday.

evidence.text: Had a great time here with some colleagues late night dinner after a long day
He was awesome very accommodating, knowledgeable about the menu and drinks were a plus…
I ordered from your late-night menu (a standard burger and Cajun fries) since that was all that was available, though I really had my heart set on a Caesar salad

reviews.text: Loved the chicken wings here. Italian hot Parm flavor was a mix of parm and hot sauce bringing out a unique flavor. Definitely try. Cool place to chill. They got tables and bar..

Had a great time here with some colleagues late night dinner after a long day. Our server was Nyil. He was awesome very accommodating, knowledgeable about the menu and drinks were a plus…. He made the best Smokey Old Fashion with candied cherries. I must’ve had 4 of them. We ordered Nachos for the table-absolutely delicious, and we all had burgers which was very tasty also.

I wanted to share my disappointment with the meal I received tonight. I ordered from your late-night menu (a standard burger and Cajun fries) since that was all that was available, though I really had my heart set on a Caesar salad.

When I got home, I found that my burger patty was extremely oversized and very salty. I had to slice it in half just to try to eat it, it was pink inside and unfortunately undercooked. To make matters worse, I discovered a hair on my tomato. The Cajun fries were also very cold, old, and inedible. It looked like I was given the bottom of the barrel since most pieces were very small.

I had heard great things about your food, so this was especially disappointing especially since it wasn’t even that late (you’re open until 2am), and I was really looking forward to enjoying my meal. I was starving, and I couldn’t even eat it. I did try calling to share my concerns, but no one answered, so I left a voicemail.

On a positive note, the gentleman who waited on me tonight was a sweetheart very attentive and kind (I wish I could remember his name). My issue isn’t with the service at the counter, but with the quality of the food I received. Y’all I cried cause ain’t nothing worst that wanted something so bad you get home and can’t even enjoy what you paid for.

I truly hope this feedback helps improve the late-night experience for future customers.

I stopped by Industry for a late dinner on a Tuesday night, and it was a pretty easy walk-in experience with no hassle. We ordered nachos for the table to start. They were good overall, though we found that there wasn’t a ton of chicken on them despite having ordered them with chicken. On the plus side, they did have plenty of other toppings.

For my main, I had the chicken sandwich. The sandwich itself was good, but the bread did get a bit soggy from the slaw and all the toppings. Still, it wasn’t bad at all—just something to be aware of if you’re not a fan of a softer bun. Overall, it was a solid late-night spot with some tasty bites!

Food was absolutely fantastic! Only downside was walking in, not getting asked about a beverage for 20 minutes, then when it was time or order (AFTER having to ask to eat) waiting an hour to get food. It was very delicious and filling but having to wait an hour and a half to get the bare minimum was ridiculous.

places.name: Cinderlands Warehouse
places.description: Elevated bar bites & house beers are served in a rustic-meets-industrial setting with a warm vibe.
places.narrative: A Strip District brewpub with serious outdoor range — photos show a tree-lined beer garden with picnic tables on gravel AND a semi-enclosed covered patio, giving you options depending on weather and mood. Reviewers praise the "great atmosphere" and mention wing specials alongside a solid beer selection. Photos show colorful, well-presented wraps and dishes — the food is more elevated than typical brewery fare. At 4.3 with 561 reviews, open until 9 PM today, 7 min away. Cocktails and wine supplement the house beers. A well-rounded pick where the dual outdoor spaces and food quality justify the drive.

evidence.text: Always a great atmosphere
Great selection of beer and food was good, wing special on Thursday
Got a 4 pack of the Fuerig Smoked Schwarzbier, a collaboration with Noble Creature Wild Ales & Lagers

reviews.text: My absolute favorite place to visit for a beer when I’m in the Strip District. Their buffalo chicken dip is also one of the best I’ve had. I’ve also attended plenty of events here that they put on and it’s always enjoyable. Always a great atmosphere! I highly recommend checking out Cinderlands!
Great selection of beer and food was good, wing special on Thursday. Got a 4 pack of the Fuerig Smoked Schwarzbier, a collaboration with Noble Creature Wild Ales & Lagers. Delicious

Glad to know Pittsburgh is doing a few things right. This brewery being one of them. It's in 'The Strip,' and don't worry, they won't have Las Vegas Strip style pricing here. There's street parking and a giant parking lot right next door. Lots of construction going on in this area. So, The Strip is up and coming? There's plenty of indoor/outdoor seating, including bar stools. Had a couple beers and read a book at the bar. Social anxiety mixed with love of craft beer. If that's you, too, expect some overhead comments like, 'I thought this was a bar,' from the sassy, heartless bartender. Discomfort!

Beer time: Tracks Again is a fine traditional pilsner. Squish Ice is a modern hop-forward West Coast pilsner. Don't see too many of those, and it's a good one. Get it while you can. Strawberry Yinzerade is a nice sour, and was the visit's taste highlight. Bombs in Pop Space, another fruited sour, had lots of terrific blended fruit flavors, softened with some lactose for that milkshake taste. The Coffee & Orange Nitro Milk Stout was gross. Not recommended. The piña colada inspired Rooftop Colada wheat beer was an unexpected treat.

My husband wanted to try the IPA's. I'm not a beer drinker and usually find breweries to have limited other options. This place has a full bar and their margarita is very good. We also loved the Red pizza and the Smoked Brisket Wrap. Both 10/10! The downstairs is bar service, just order from the table and they bring it out, there's cornhole and a few other tabletop games set up. Upstairs is table service with a section of open air seating!

Where to even start? I visited Cinderlands Warehouse and it was amazing! Truly a gem—gorgeous space, really good beer and cocktails, and the food? Absolutely delicious.
The place has two floors and a deck for outdoor seating, which is perfect when the weather’s nice. Since this is where they brew their beer, I had to try something local. I went with the Lil Cinder Mango—a classic American light lager made with real mango purée and flavor. It’s the perfect summer sipper!
Also tried Cindi’s Hard Mountain Tea, and as a fan of all things iced tea, this was a dream. It’s a hard iced tea, steam brewed and fizz-free, served over ice—super refreshing.
From the bites menu, we had:
Cheese curds: perfectly crispy, served with marinara.
Brussels sprouts: sunflower pesto, cherry tomatoes, couscous, aged provolone, and pistachios. This flavor combo was out of this world—truly a standout dish.
We happened to go on a Thursday, which meant Wing Night—tip: mark your calendar! Wings are just $1 each, available in 6 or 12-piece orders. The dry rub flavor was delicious.
We also tried a variety of mains:
Red Pizza: a classic—marinara with a blend of cheddar, fontina, and parmesan. Simple and so good.
Crunch Wrap: shredded beef, Fritos, beer cheese, enchilada sauce, and Aleppo sour cream. Absolutely delicious.
Smashed Wagyu Burger: two wagyu patties with grilled onions, dijonnaise, American cheese, bread & butter pickles, all on a Mediterra challah bun. Super fresh and tasty. All sandwiches come with chips too!
Cinderlands has a few locations around the city, and they also sell their beer in bars and through local distributors. But the Warehouse location? Highly recommend checking it out!

places.name: Arsenal Cider House & Wine Cellar
places.narrative: Not a brewery — this is a cider house and wine cellar, so no beer on tap. But the outdoor space is special: reviewers call the cider garden out back "a pleasant surprise and great place for a casual date night." Live music too. At 4.8 with 707 reviews, it's clearly beloved. Open until 4 PM today, 5 min away. If cider and wine work instead of beer, this offers arguably the most atmospheric outdoor drinking experience on this list. Jess might appreciate the chill garden vibe, but Robbie would miss his IPA. Know what you're signing up for.

evidence.text: Also, the cider garden out back was a pleasant surprise and great place for a casual date night
Great 1st time vist
All were excellent, as was the food

reviews.text: Great spot! They offered us sample size tastes to aid in choosing a cider. We ended up going with their classic Archebald's and for me it was the perfect blend of sweet, tart, and slightly fizzy. Also, the cider garden out back was a pleasant surprise and great place for a casual date night. We came in the afternoon before the main crowd. Finally, just have to say the ladies restroom was spotless. Definitely would recommend.
Great 1st time vist. Such a cool house and the history of how Arsenal Cider started. Cider is good!
13 types of cider on tap and more bottled. Can try 3 samples per person before purchase. All were excellent, as was the food. The Cubano was on- point!

This is the perfect place for a low-key, catch-up with friends and family. My current favorite cider is the Grant's Pumpkin. It tastes like fall in a cup! The pretzels were brushed with garlic butter, they didn't last long enough for a pic. The Ruben was incredible I would recommend for anyone who likes Rubens. You will not be disappointed!

Talk about an awesome spot for a cider drinker like myself. I happened upon this place as I was having dinner down the street and friends mentioned this place and we decided to mosey on over. We were able to taste a few ciders and I left with two bottles. I highly recommend

places.name: The Porch
places.description: Laid-back gathering place for seasonal menus crafted using ingredients from local producers.
places.narrative: Sitting right at the edge of Schenley Park, this farm-to-table spot serves seasonal menus with local ingredients. Photos show a spacious patio with metal chairs, wooden tables, and large shade trees — one of the more polished outdoor setups around. Reviewers mention wagyu burgers and note "everything on the menu sounded good." At 4.1 with 2,130 reviews, the rating is the lowest among close-by options — service seems to be the common gripe. Open until 8 PM, just 3 min away, with live music, full bar, and coffee. The park-adjacent location is the selling point — pair it with a Schenley walk.

evidence.text: Everything on the menu sounded good
I ordered the wagyu burger and fries and my friend got the grilled cheese and tomato soup
But once we received our food and drinks that's the last we seen our server

reviews.text:
This is a very nice restaurant.  Looks clean and cozy.  Everything on the menu sounded good. I ordered the wagyu burger and fries and my friend got the grilled cheese and tomato soup.  The good looked good and tasted delicious.  But once we received our food and drinks that's the last we seen our server.  No check ins or refills.  That was disappointing.
Table had 5 plates 5 sets of silverware and 5 glasses on it when we sat down.  They were never removed.  Sat on the table our whole visit.

Went to The Porch for brunch and I’m glad we did. Right on the campus of the University of Pittsburgh this place is a definite recommendation. We decided to get a pitcher of the Bloody Mary and it did not disappoint. The food was fabulous with multiple seasonal options. For a light lunch the salmon wrap was fantastic with a great flavor profile. Parking took a little while to find however after finding street parking the meal made the walk over worth it.

This is overall a phenomenal spot for lunch or dinner, located right on Pitt's campus. The restaurant has a modern feeling, with both indoor and outdoor seating overlooking a bright green field of grass. Menu is varied, with something to please just about anyone. The restaurant was very clean, and the staff was friendly as well. With fair pricing on top of this, it is hard to say no.

We came hear to eat with a bunch of people (~20) after a conference at CMU. We had our own two tables. The place was buzzing, but it was still quiet enough to talk. The food itself was excellent. Service was kind and attentive.

I went several weeks ago and had the most wonderful server for brunch named Isabella. She was so friendly and kind and knew so much about the menu. I told her I like to eat a lot and she recommended the butternut squash pizza with prosciutto. OMG, it was SO delicious. Thank you Isabella for the great service and amazing recommendation! 🍕

places.name: Hazelwood Brew House
places.narrative: A stunning Hazelwood multi-brewery complex in a historic building — reviewers describe a "beautiful space with great views" featuring a ground-floor outdoor tasting area, a third-floor tap room, and a rooftop beer garden. Photos confirm a dramatic elevated deck with sunset views over rolling hills — easily the most scenic outlook on this entire list. Multiple breweries under one roof plus a comfort food spot means variety. At 4.9 with 109 reviews, open until 6 PM today, 7 min away. The rooftop with those views is hard to find elsewhere. A genuine wow-factor destination.

evidence.text: The Hazelwood Brewhouse is a beautiful space with great views and two (previously three) decent breweries plus a comfort food place
There is a small, outdoor tasting area on the ground floor for all 3 spaces and then a larger 3rd floor tap room for all 3 spaces, plus a rooftop beer garden
Great outdoor space with a rooftop area with a great view, additional floors that will be open soon, and a dog-friendly patio when you first walk up

reviews.text: The Hazelwood Brewhouse is a beautiful space with great views and two (previously three) decent breweries plus a comfort food place. It is MASSIVELY overbuilt and not very well known— as a result, pints run $8-10 on average. Still worth checking out for a drink before heading to Hazel Grove.

Here at Hazelwood Brew House is Abstract Brew Company and New France Brewing Company. There is supposed to be a 3rd Brewing Company in this complex, but sadly they have closed entirely. They are hoping to have a 3rd in Q1 2025. Both offer a wide variety of brews. I enjoyed the Blindfold Belgian Tripel at New France and the Killer Cobra Imperial Cream Ale at Abstract. Awesome location. There is a small, outdoor tasting area on the ground floor for all 3 spaces and then a larger 3rd floor tap room for all 3 spaces, plus a rooftop beer garden. Definitely worth checking out.

Just came across this today, and it did not disappoint. Three breweries in one really cool space. Great outdoor space with a rooftop area with a great view, additional floors that will be open soon, and a dog-friendly patio when you first walk up. The brew house is located right off the bike path, easily accessible from Hot Metal Bridge. They had a food truck while we were there, so you can get a bite to eat, too. Looking forward to biking here and enjoying the space again!

If you want a fun evening with friends, this is the place to go. There are 2 micro breweries serving totally different styles of beer. 1 has wonderful lagers. We had the MaiBock, smooth and on point.  The other brewery had a refreshing oatmeal coconut stout.
We had the steak salad with arugula greens dressed in a light vinegarette, while our friends had the mac & cheese and nachos.
We were also there for trivia night. We came in 4th... but 3 teams were tied for first. Does that make us second place? Not sure. Check out the roof top also while you are there.

The space is awesome. Water cups on the way out! Good thinking.

La France had beers I really liked; Abstract Realm had a tasty stout. Abjurgation is on deck; sent a message to get a ballpark date but no response yet.

It will be very interesting to see what kind of food options they'll add.

places.name: Burghers Brewing Co.
places.narrative: A Lawrenceville pub that's essentially all outdoors — reviewers note "there is really no indoor seating" and warn it can be tough in extreme weather. Photos show a charming courtyard between industrial brick buildings with bistro tables, planters, and string lights, plus burger-and-fries on rustic wood. Beer only, no cocktails or wine. Dog-friendly, open until 8 PM today, 6 min away. At 4.3 with just 49 reviews, it's small and casual. Great on a nice day like today, but have a backup plan since there's essentially no indoor fallback if weather turns.

evidence.text: There is really no indoor seating
So if it’s very cold or hot, it would be a little hard to eat here
I liked the food and service was very nice

reviews.text:
There is really no indoor seating. So if it’s very cold or hot, it would be a little hard to eat here . They have benches that are covered, very small indoor area, and a bathroom. Water or soft drinks come in bottle/can.
I liked the food and service was very nice. We got the liberty smash burger 🍔. Fries were good too. Overall I really liked the concept and their food! $50 for two people including tip.

I just had the best meal and beers here. The beer garden concept is great too! They have a tv outside where a game could be put on. The brewmaster really knows what he is doing because everything was very close to Bavarian favorites that I enjoy in Europe. The staff was very friendly too! The burger was amazing, and I never knew I was missing out with pierogis on the side. Loving it here! I will be back!

Wow, Burghers was amazing! We enjoyed lunch here after a campus tour at Duquesne University. The BBBG team took time to understand my food allergies. They prepared my meal with care and kindness! The Green Tree Bowl was delicious and safe. My family thoroughly enjoyed their burgers and fries. The garden and music selection perfectly complimented the experience. Thank you!!

We had a smashing good time at Burghers Beer Garden with Brittany! It was our 2nd stop on a brewery tour and it was by far the best! We sampled all 10 beers + a bonus beer. They were all excellent. The burgers, fries & pierogis were delicious. And the service was top notch. I only wish we were not out of towners and could make this our regular hang out.

If you’re on a never-ending quest for the best smash burger like I was, STOP RIGHT NOW — the burger gods have answered. We hit up this convenient little burger spot and it was everything: food hot ash, right iff the grill…. music so good you almost forget you’re stuffing your face, and customer service that felt like being welcomed by an old friend who also happens to know their way around a flat top grill.

We got two Oakland burgers (smashed to absolute perfection), fries so crispy they could be  ASMR content, Joe’s Peach Tea (elite), a bottle of classic Root Beer (Red Ribbon knows what’s up), mojo sauce, AND burgher sauce. Picky boyfriend approved — and trust me, that’s harder to accomplish than finding a parking spot in Southside on a Saturday night.

The person running the place? Cool as hell. The type of cool where you instantly want to be friends. We didn’t just eat — we demolished every last crumb. If you leave even a fry behind, you’re doing life wrong.

Final Verdict:
10/10. Best smash burger I’ve had after months of searching.
“Oh yea we’re definitely coming back…” words of the picky boyfriend (2 bites in)
