places.name: Inner Groove Brewing - Pittsburgh Taproom
places.full_address: 827 E Warrington Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15210, USA
places.narrative: A Warrington Ave taproom where reviewers highlight the beer garden as "great in the summer to bring games and pizza" — and the BYOF (bring your own food) policy is a unique perk. Photos show a cozy beer garden with picnic tables and string lights in an alleyway between buildings. Easy parking with a private lot. At 4.8 with 34 reviews, it's small and new-ish but the flexibility to grab takeout from somewhere amazing and pair it with their craft beer is genuinely appealing. Open until 7 PM today, 9 min away.

evidence.text: The location is easy to park with a private lot behind the building and they allow you to bring in your own food
The patio/beer garden is great in the summer to bring games and pizza and hang out
Have only been a few times but the staff are always incredibly welcoming and the beer is always solid with a great variety

reviews.text:
My favorite brewery in this city. They have something for everyone but this time of year is my favorite beer.
The hallowed ground  pumpkin ale is my all time favorite, with the gingerbell coming in 2nd.  My boyfriend likes all sours.
The location is easy to park with a private lot behind the building and they allow you to bring in your own food. The patio/beer garden is great in the summer to bring games and pizza and hang out. We love this place and will always return.
Have only been a few times but the staff are always incredibly welcoming and the beer is always solid with a great variety.
Really chill. Had a guy playing an accordion for the evening. Nothing but vibes.
We went for the Mario kart tournament. First time there and everyone was so friendly and the beer is great. They have pretzels but can bring food!

I enjoyed my time here. They serve up brews and have other events like trivia and chili cookoffs (there is no food here otherwise). Service was great and the brews are better than what I've had at other places. They also have a patio for when it's warmer. I'd come back when in the area

places.name: New Amsterdam
places.description: Industrial hangout offering finger foods & lots of microbrews, plus local art & a rooftop patio bar.
places.narrative: An industrial Lawrenceville hangout with microbrews, local art, and a rooftop patio bar — reviewers were surprised by the food quality, saying "didn't expect high end, delicious food" and "the food was too good." Photos show an outdoor beer garden between brick buildings with high-top tables, string lights, and open sky. Full bar with cocktails, wine, coffee, plus live music. At 4.1 with 772 reviews, the rating is modest but the food praise is unexpectedly strong. Open until 10 PM today, 6 min away. The rooftop angle and surprisingly good food make this an underrated pick.

evidence.text: The food was too good
Didn't expect high end, delicious food
The drink called "chef's kiss" lived up to its name for sure

reviews.text: I was there for music bingo this tuesday and had an unforgettable experience. Bunny the bartender was so nice and talkative which i love. The food was too good. sinful! Try the Elotè wings. best wings i’ve ever had in my entire life.

Just came in for a beer and watch the game. Didn't expect high end, delicious food! Didn't go upstairs, younger crowded navigated that way. Outstanding customer service, the wings and mac cheese were amazing. So many house made sauces it was hard to decide on which ones. Alabama white bbq with scorpion seasoning was our favorite. What stole the show was perfect, and I do mean perfect,  pork belly appetizer! Next time we're in town, we will be back!

Fantastic drinks and super cute upstairs space for hanging out! The drink called "chef's kiss" lived up to its name for sure. It was pretty busy but the service was super quick and the bartenders were nice. One of them even complimented my dress which made me so happy!

Love the new look! Nicely done 👍 the drinks are fun and the menu 😋 Hawaiian food!! Some dishes I never had and well made. The food is provided on plastic plates however it’s a bar. Totally understandable. Fun. Great selections of beer. Great music. The staff is kind. The food didn’t take long and the prices are right. Parking can be tricky. You just have to get lucky. But totally worth it. Love the roof top. Took my HS son for lunch and then another time for dinner with friends. They can also host private events, something to consider. Not handicap friendly. If you can definitely check it out. Kids okay during the day, I wouldn’t do evenings. Gets crowded and more of a bar scene.

We stopped after work for a bite and a fe drinks. Low crowd so the service was top notch. They have an upstairs and a downstairs but I didnt brave it.  Wide selection of beers and the food was awesome. Dont skip the curry poutine fries and their billionaire burger was delicious!

places.name: Four Points Brewing Taproom
places.narrative: A North Side brewery where reviewers praise "great atmosphere, beer, and music" and note food comes via rotating trucks and popup events throughout the week. Photos show a patio with picnic tables under open sky. At 4.7 with 108 reviews, open until 6 PM today, but 11 min away. Beer-only drink menu. The food truck model means you'll want to check what's rolling today before committing to the drive. A solid community brewery that rewards the trip when the stars align — good truck, good weather, good company.

evidence.text: Great atmosphere, beer, and music - can’t go wrong
Throughout the week they have food trucks or popup food events
Great location on the North Shore

reviews.text: Four points has quickly moved into our favorite brewery to visit in the city. We haven’t had a beer we don’t like and the bartenders have been incredible each time, so kind! Also have appreciated that they’ve been family friendly. Being newly postpartum, you hope to find spaces you used to enjoy that still work for your family - and they have been nothing short of amazing in making us feel we belong. Great atmosphere, beer, and music - can’t go wrong!

The best part about this place is that they offer Surfside spiked teas. I don’t drink beer and I am always so happy when a brewery serves Surfsides!!! Thank you! Oh and my husband says the beer is really good.

This is a really cool local bar on the Northside. The beers are all made in-house and taste amazing. You can sit at the bar or in the back where there are couches and pinball machines. Throughout the week they have food trucks or popup food events.

Great location on the North Shore. Cool indoor relaxed space with some comfy couches and pinball and a newly added outdoor patio. The beer line up is solid. They have lots of different styles, and all have been on point. They don't have food, but food trucks are sometimes on site. They also offer pitchers of beer, which is rare for breweries. Four packs available to go.

Went down to the northside to go to War streets brewing (Piers Pub) and happily found that Four points opened a taproom within a block.
Four points had 10 different beers with pretty much something for everyone. I had two IPAs and both were outstanding. I particularly liked the “Kids” IPA, around 5.5% and very hazy.
The place was large with lots of room to move around and they had an outdoor space.
It’s pretty cool that there’s three breweries within one block of each other, Four points, War Street brewing, and 412.

places.name: Aslin Beer Company
places.narrative: The Strip District outpost of the Virginia-born brewery chain, where reviewers call it "really good food options for a brewery spot" — specifically praising thin-crust, crispy pizza with creative toppings. Photos show a front patio with awning and plated dishes. At 4.0 with 354 reviews, it's the lowest-rated actual brewery on this list, which is notable. Open until 10 PM today, 8 min away. The in-house food kitchen (not just trucks) is a genuine differentiator, and the pizza specifically gets consistent praise even if the overall rating suggests inconsistency elsewhere.

evidence.text: Really good food options for a brewery spot
Their pizza is thin crust, crispy with some nice topping combination options
The only kinda miss was the fries, which weren’t really crispy and were just okay, but would say the pizza is worth trying

reviews.text: Really good food options for a brewery spot! Their pizza is thin crust, crispy with some nice topping combination options. Brussels sprouts were also worth it, actually crispy with a nice sauce too. The only kinda miss was the fries, which weren’t really crispy and were just okay, but would say the pizza is worth trying!

The food is decent but I suspect it would improve if they limited their menu. Pizza, burgers, Korean options, and pasta is possibly too many options to deliver uniformly great outcomes.

The sliders were mediocre at best; it was a full-size patty cut into quarters. Just remove sliders from the menu, in my opinion, if this is going to be how you expand your menu. The mushroom pizza was good but not great. Too much crust. The hot dog was decent and I recommend it.

The carry-out can selection on November 28, 2025 consisted of many passable cans and only one DIPA; it almost seems like a conglomerate of their less-enticing 12oz distro beers and the less-popular one-offs from the past few months. Another DIPA would have been nice. Perhaps a stout.

I love fest bier and Märzen lager, but still available for carry-out in the last three days of November?  I suspect the administration is potentially struggling with projecting demand. In their defense, it must be tough in a town that has a segment that loves light beer but another that prefers barrel-aged stouts. And many others.

There were no draft BA-stouts on November 28. Or any (alcoholic) stouts.

Staff is great; very nice. The drinks arrive fast.

We will come back, but we liked the options better November 2024.

Really lovely interior and nice seating outside.  And the staff bring you drinks really fast.

The drinks aren't the best (a little sour for my taste, but that's subjective and you might like them).  They aren't that expensive, though.  The food is a bit pricey.

There's one main negative experience I've had here.  I took my family from out of state to Aslin because it was one of my favorite breweries due to the location/vibe.  A couple of us were getting beers + food there sitting at one of the outdoor tables.  My little sister has a severe dairy allergy, so her and some other folks got some food from a restaurant down the street that doesn't use any milk products.  To be fair to Aslin: there are notes on the outdoor tables saying no outside food.  And our waiter didn't know about the allergy.  But when one of the staff brought out a drink, they forced us to leave or throw away the food.  It left a bad taste in my mouth and I haven't been back since.

This is THE spot. Happy hour deals are great (a bunch of sliders for $10 and huge beers), and it’s got a beautiful view of the city. Would love to see a happy hour rotation of one of their stronger beers every now and then, but that’s just me being picky. If you can get here before 5pm and grab an outside table, it’s the spot to be in the strip. Love it

I visited this place for the first time with a few friends, located inside the new Strip District Terminal. We were lucky to find parking right outside the terminal. Although we wanted outdoor seating, we ended up inside, which was a fun experience with great music.

The beer selection was fantastic and enjoyable, with plenty of options to choose from. We ordered pizza—the pepperoni and ricotta was a big hit with our group, though the buffalo chicken didn’t win everyone over.

I liked that we could order through ToastTab, and the food and beer were brought out quickly! The system was easy to use, and you can keep the tab open to add more items—perfect for large groups so you can order separately.

However, one major downside was that the indoor area was super cold—it was almost uncomfortably chilly! Definitely bring a jacket if you’re planning to sit inside. Overall, a great spot, but they really need to address the indoor temperature.

places.name: Burghers Brewing Company Lawrenceville Tap House
places.description: Upbeat spot offering build-your-own burgers & other locally sourced fare, plus shakes & sodas.
places.narrative: The Lawrenceville Tap House sibling of Burghers Brewing, focused on build-your-own burgers with locally sourced ingredients. Here's the dealbreaker: outdoor seating is listed as unavailable, which misses the query entirely. Photos show nachos and pub food; reviewers mention grilled cheese with four kinds of cheese (not great for Carissa or Ashi). At 4.2 with 692 reviews, it's decent. Beer, cocktails, wine, and coffee — a full drink menu. But without outdoor seating, this only works as a rainy-day backup. The burger customization concept is fun though.

evidence.text: Tried the grilled cheese
Was great four kinds of cheese on toast with a tomato and pickles
Burgh'ers in Lawrenceville is a great place for burgers and beer

reviews.text:
Stopped by to pass some time.  Tried the Aufstoin. Awesome doughy malt lager.  Tried the grilled cheese.  Was great four kinds of cheese on toast with a tomato and pickles.  Added pickled onions.  Yummy.

Also have had blended mushroom beef patty burgers and the fries never disappoint.

This was probably the best smash burger I have had in the city! The flavors were off the charts and the fries had the perfect crisp on them. Our waitress was very kind and attentive to our needs. We were there earlier in the afternoon so it wasn’t too busy which was nice. Would highly recommend checking this spot out!

Burgh'ers in Lawrenceville is a great place for burgers and beer. It's a casual, industrial spot with friendly staff.
I had the Oakland burger and it was perfectly cooked and included locally sourced toppings.
I didn't try any of the beers, but they had an impressive selection with house brewed options.
You can also get a Mini Smash if you have less of an appetite.

Good food. Watch your receipt. Prices don't match the menu. I ordered the morningside $15 with chilli mac $4 charged $20. Originally server didn't give me fries. The menu clearly states "upgrade your fries." I took the dollar discrepancy out of the tip.

The least busiest of the breweries we visited, but it was the most interaction we got with staff, a big plus in my book...

From the outside it was non-desript, but the inside revealed a sizeable taproom/restaurant setup with a decent sized bar to go along with it all.  Though we did not eat here, we could see they had a nice sized menu and it was made to order.

For beers we had each a lager and a dunkel, very good offerings that came in nice cone-shaped glassware - definitely out of the ordinary.  Service was spot on and super friendly as we shared our experiences on the day and they genuinely were receptive to the whole discussion.

Though it was a little hard to find, it was worth the effort and definitely worth a return trip..

places.name: Spoonwood Brewing Company
places.narrative: Arguably the best overall brewery-with-patio package on this list when it's open — photos show a large beer garden with string lights AND a spacious patio with umbrellas and greenery. Reviewers praise both food and atmosphere, with attentive service called out by name. At 4.5 with 841 reviews, it's well-proven. Two big catches: it's closed today (Sunday) and it's 20 min away in Bethel Park. Bookmark this for another day — the beer garden setup is genuinely compelling and the food gets real praise, not just "it's fine for a brewery."

evidence.text: Our food server, Trish, was quick, thorough and helpful
Great food and fun atmosphere
Great beers, space, service and food

reviews.text: Brunch this morning at Spoonwood Brewing was wonderful! The Eggs Benedict was perfectly cooked and the hollandaise sauce was delicious. My husband and I shared the Waffle of the Day - the Cinnamon Toast Crunch. Surprisingly it wasn’t overly sweet. It was an airy, wonderful waffle. Cindy was our wait staff and she was friendly, attentive and even brought cinnamon sticks for my chai tea. Our food server, Trish, was quick, thorough and helpful. Take home an growler of beer for later, too! Excellent brunch!

We had a lovely Sunday brunch. The staff was professional, attentive and personable. Our meals were delicious and I can’t say enough about the potable potions we had with our meal. Great food and fun atmosphere. A gem in Bethel Park.
Great beers, space, service and food! Very spacious, cool vibes, many TVs for sports viewing and nice looking outdoor section. Will come back when in the area :)

Never had a bad meal here. And the selection of beer is great. We are not into IPA's and many other places we've been to tend to have more of them, whereas Spoonwood offers a bigger variety.  My favorite by far was the Secret Alphabet made with honey, oranges,  jalapeño and habenero peppers.
The Jam Burger was tasty and cocktail menu (rainbow marg specifically) was delicious! Exceptionally busy on a Saturday night with no parking. The earlier you get there the better!

places.name: Back Alley Brewing Company
places.full_address: 2975 W Liberty Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15216, USA
places.narrative: Way out in Dormont at 16 min away — the most distant open option. The 4.8 rating from 92 reviews is strong though, with reviewers praising staff warmth and the flexible space — it's popular for private events and parties. No outdoor photos captured despite outdoor seating being listed. Open until 8 PM today. At this distance, you'd need a specific reason to choose it over closer options unless you're already on that side of town. More of a gathering-and-event space than a drop-in brewery destination.

evidence.text: And I know I already said this, but Lee was just great to work with
We rented out Back Alley for our daughters birthday party and I highly recommend it for anyone looking for a great event space with flexibility and good beer
There is typically a food truck outside too

reviews.text: We rented Back Alley Brewing for a shower, and it was perfect! Lots of natural light, lots of tables, the cutest greenery draped across the ceiling, super friendly staff that was wonderful to work with, pretty affordable. Highly recommend! And I know I already said this, but Lee was just great to work with. He was responsive to emails, easy-going, and friendly. We rented out the right side of the brewery, which is a pretty segmented off room (but without doors). Our group was just under 40 people, and it was comfortable.

Back Alley Brewing is a very nice little brewery. We hosted my wife's 40th birthday party there and it was the perfect space for about 30 people. I think you could have up to 40 somewhat comfortably. The beers were really good. I'm not an IPA guy so I had the coffee stout and the lager; both very good! I highly recommend this place to have a few beers or to have a get-together.

We rented out Back Alley for our daughters birthday party and I highly recommend it for anyone looking for a great event space with flexibility and good beer! The Back Alley team was super accomodating and communicative throughout the process. The beer was excellent and the bartenders was incredibly attentive and helpful.

Fabulous brewery. Came into town Saturday and this was first stop. Loved the Goldenrod Autumn Shandy and bought a 4pack to go of the Back Alley IPA. Enjoyed this little gem of a brewery so much we went back Sunday too. My husband and I shared 2 flights so we could try nearly all of their beers. Fluffernut pumpkin beer was also very good. Will definitely be back next time we're in Pittsburgh. Beers are solid
This is such a fun location to visit! Bright and airy inside with a wide range of beers on tap to enjoy. There is typically a food truck outside too.
